newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak blue chips mixed, SAX eases 2.1 pts.
newsitem.headline: Slovak blue chips mixed, SAX eases 2.1 pts.

text.p: Most major Slovak issues closed higher in flat session on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Monday, with losses to share of Chemolak dragging the SAX index down 2.1 points.
Since the beginning of this year, the BSE changed technical rules in dealing in block trades on the bourse floor, and brokers said it was cutting back the volume of trade.

"The new three-minute ask rule has made block trades risky as more bidders can enter the trade," said Dusan Sykora of ING Barings. The rule says a bid must remain on the visual display system at least three minutes before it can be matched by an offer.
Sykora said this change has indirectly forced a lot of deals to among the outside the bourse-direct trades.
"We see much more activity on the field of direct trades, but however, they (direct deals) are still following the trends on the floor," he added.
Oil refinery Slovnaft closed five crowns lower at 690, on a volume of 175 shares, but traded at a 0.14 percent higher average price.
Steel maker VSZ closed up nine at 640, with 132 traded shares. Paint producer Chemolak closed 300 crowns lower at 1,450, dragging the bourse index down, but on only three shares traded.
"I think most of blue chips will rise in the near future, with prices boosted by strong demand, but let's not expect any spectacular volumes," Sykora added.
Overall volume eased to 116,600 shares, from 383,108 shares traded on Friday, and turnover decreased to 98.85 million crowns, from 181.17 million. -- Peter Javurek, Bratislava Newsroom, 42-7-563-3687
